source.title: Gradient Descent on Neural Networks Typically Occurs at the Edge of Stability
source.authors: Jeremy M. Cohen; Simran Kaur; Yuanzhi Li; J. Kolter; A. Talwalkar

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly runs full-batch gradient descent and measures training loss and Hessian sharpness relative to the 2/η stability threshold, the behavior described in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper tests edge-of-stability behavior in full-batch gradient descent. Results it cites from Lewkowycz et al. are prior work, not this study’s own results. The batch-normalization comparison also bears on V6.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures full-batch training loss and Hessian sharpness relative to 2/η, testing V5's sustained edge-of-stability behavior. Its controlled BN comparison also tests V6's training-speed component.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: full-batch GD commonly exhibits progressive sharpening followed by threshold hovering and longer-term loss decrease despite short-term oscillations. The authors explicitly qualify this characterization across losses, architectures, and measurement choices, and leave its mechanism and extension to SGD unresolved. Their matched CNN experiment also confirms BN acceleration.
record.recipe_differences: The study directly measures full-batch gradient descent dynamics and Hessian sharpness relative to 2/η; it does not test the above-initial-stability-limit catapult recipe described in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The edge-of-stability pattern is reported across step sizes, losses, architectures, and tasks. Cross-entropy sharpness often drops near the end of training; BN networks require measuring sharpness between iterates at very small step sizes; width, depth, and dataset size change the degree of progressive sharpening.

fits_no_version.finding: BN and non-BN networks have similar sharpness and effective smoothness near 2/η when effective smoothness is measured at the actual training-step distance; deep-linear comparisons change when measured at 30 times that distance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN need not accelerate training by reducing sharpness or effective smoothness along the optimization trajectory.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD can alternate between expected increases and decreases in full-dataset loss, with the sign changing under hypothetical learning-rate or batch-size changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD acclimates to its learning rate and batch size in its expected one-step loss change.

record.problems: The central evidence is empirical and many results are shown in figures without exact values. For BN comparison, training-speed values are not reported numerically. Standard CIFAR-10 sharpness is approximated using only the first 5,000 examples (or first five BN batches).
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results omitted. Results cited from Lewkowycz et al. and other prior work were not extracted as this study’s own findings.

untested.parts: The stated SGD/Adam classification-error claim, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and comparisons involving size, early stopping, and regularization are not tested. The reported full-batch GD completion results do not establish those conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student overparameterization.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation, matched identity-shortcut comparisons, very deep plain tanh training, and Fixup.
Comparisons of activation-matched initializations, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, and initialization-dependent trainable depth.

The above-initial-stability-limit catapult regime, its larger-rate divergence boundary, and the later Gilmer et al. instability result. Contrary to the record, sustained threshold hovering during longer-term loss decrease is directly tested.
Higher learning-rate tolerance is not established by the matched-step CNN speed comparison. The listed MNIST and ImageNet settings and Fixup's normalization-free training recipe are not tested.

missing.what: V5's architecture coverage and qualifications: additional fully connected and convolutional architectures reproduce threshold hovering; ReLU and hardtanh networks sometimes plateau below 2/η. These exceptions are absent from the rows.
BN measurement dependence: at small step sizes, iterate sharpness can plateau below 2/η while maximum sharpness between successive iterates reaches the threshold.
missing.locator: Appendices A.4 and K; Figures 71 and 73

missing.what: Additional task results: WikiText-2 Transformer threshold hovering with continued loss progress; degree-5 Chebyshev regression temporarily stalls before monotone improvement; deep-linear loss is largely monotone except for a brief blip.
Cross-entropy sharpness often falls near training completion, qualifying the duration of threshold hovering.
missing.locator: Sections 3.1–3.2; Appendices A.1 and C; Figures 5, 10–11

missing.what: After learning-rate reductions, sharpness resumes rising toward the new 2/η threshold or until training ends.

record.verdict_notes: No V5 verdict labels are assigned because this study is an original source for V5. Its full-batch restriction is already part of that version and is not itself a scope limitation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach near-zero classification error, including with corrupted or random labels, or compare smaller models and regularized recipes.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiments or width comparisons.
Does not compare plain networks with and without identity shortcuts for training error, or test Fixup.
Does not compare activation-matched, Gaussian, or orthogonal initializations for training speed or trainable depth.

Does not test the catapult mechanism described by Lewkowycz et al. at rates above the initial linearized-model stability limit. It studies full-batch gradient descent at and beyond the evolving 2/η threshold, not whether sharpness hovers at the threshold during longer-time loss decrease.
Tests whether batch normalization accelerates training in one ReLU CNN comparison, but does not test higher learning-rate tolerance across the listed model families or Fixup.

rows.subject: fully-connected architecture with two hidden layers of width 200, and tanh activations
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with MSE classification loss, stopped at 99% training accuracy.
rows.measure: Training loss and Hessian sharpness relative to 2/η during training.
rows.value: The sharpness continually rises while remaining beneath 2/η; training is stopped at 99% accuracy.
rows.note: This small-step-size run deliberately keeps sharpness below the threshold; it does not test the above-threshold V5 behavior.
rows.check: Valid small-step control: sharpness remains below 2/η throughout training. This does not establish absence of the threshold-hovering effect in runs that reach the threshold.

rows.subject: fully-connected architecture with two hidden layers of width 200, and tanh activations
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with MSE classification loss at several step sizes.
rows.measure: Training loss pattern after sharpness first crosses 2/η.
rows.baseline: Training loss decreases monotonically before the breakeven point.
rows.value: After the breakeven point, training loss behaves non-monotonically over short timescales yet decreases consistently over long timescales.
rows.note: The text describes the pattern across a range of step sizes; individual plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Add the accompanying sharpness plateau at or just above 2/η. Figure 5 includes both MSE and cross-entropy; the row currently records only MSE.

rows.subject: VGG with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent at a range of step sizes; trained to completion.
rows.measure: Training loss pattern and sharpness after sharpness reaches 2/η.
rows.value: The training loss behaves non-monotonically yet consistently decreases over long timescales, while sharpness hovers at or just above 2/η.
rows.locator: Appendix M, §I.2; Figures 89–90; text preceding Figure 89
rows.note: The paper reports the common pattern for the three standard architectures; this row records the VGG with BN separately.
rows.check: Specify cross-entropy and ghost BN with 50 fixed batches of 1,000. Sharpness is estimated using the first five batches. Section I.2 identifies VGG-11, despite the inconsistent VGG-19 caption in Figure 7.3.

rows.subject: VGG with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow approximated with Runge-Kutta, trained to 99% accuracy.
rows.measure: Maximum sharpness along the gradient-flow trajectory and implied stable step-size training cost.
rows.value: Sharpness rises from 6.38 at initialization to a peak value of 2227.6; the text estimates 16,622 iterations at the largest stable step size versus 329 iterations at η = 0.16.
rows.locator: Appendix M, Figure 89 and accompanying text
rows.note: This measures sharpness growth and training speed, not the V5 edge-of-stability loss pattern.
rows.check: The gradient-flow sharpness measurement is a comparator for V5, not a direct measurement of threshold hovering. Separate the observed 329-iteration GD result from the inferred lower bound of 16,622 stable-step iterations. Appendix M inconsistently reports completion time as 15.66 while calculating with 14.91.

rows.subject: ReLU CNN without batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent; compared with a ReLU CNN using batch normalization at the same step sizes.
rows.measure: Training speed, compared with the batch-normalized network.
rows.baseline: BN network trains faster at each step size.
rows.value: Figure-only comparison; no numeric speed values stated.
rows.note: Authors explicitly say the BN network trains faster for each step size; exact values are only plotted.
rows.check: The non-BN comparator establishes the same observed BN speed advantage as R8; its state should not be partial. Replace the circular baseline with the matched BN condition and record the authors' explicit qualitative speed comparison.
